title: Aamir Khan Is Getting Married Again. The Love Story Is Better Than Most Bollywood Scripts.
excerpt: A July 5 wedding, a Bangalore-born bride whose grandfather chose India over Britain, and a 25-year friendship that nobody saw turning into this.
body:
**Aamir Khan** and **Gauri Spratt** walked through Mumbai airport on Wednesday morning hand in hand, looking like a couple who had stopped pretending they had anything to hide. He was in head-to-toe black — cap, T-shirt, trousers, signature spectacles. She was in a navy-blue co-ord, elegant and unhurried. When the paparazzi swarmed, Aamir pulled down his mask and said, simply: *"Arey beti ko ghar leke jana hai yaar, please."*

The man who once vanished from all social media to prep for a single role could not outrun the biggest love story of Bollywood's summer.

Three weeks from now, on **July 5**, Aamir Khan will marry Gauri Spratt in a quiet registered ceremony at his home in Mumbai. No spectacle. No filmi extravagance. Just their two families, a handful of close friends, and a new chapter that has been unfolding behind closed doors for over a year.

> "The news about the marriage is true. It's on July 5." — Aamir Khan, to Variety India

This will be Aamir's third marriage. He was married to **Reena Dutta** from 1986 to 2002 — they share son **Junaid** and daughter **Ira Khan** — and to filmmaker **Kiran Rao** from 2005 until their separation in 2021. He and Rao continue to co-parent their son **Azad**. But the story of how Aamir found Gauri is the kind of thing that would get a greenlight at any production house in Mumbai — not for its drama, but for its patient, almost accidental grace.

**They have known each other for twenty-five years.** Not twenty-five months. Twenty-five years. They met, stayed loosely in touch, lived entirely separate lives, and then reconnected by accident. As Aamir described it on Raj Shamani's podcast:

> "Before I met Gauri, I felt like I had aged, and who will I find at this age? My therapy started, and I understood that I need to love myself first. So I worked on that." — Aamir Khan

And then Gauri happened to be in Mumbai, and they met again, and something shifted. *"We connected and became friends, and love happened. I thought I had my mother, kids, siblings — so many close relationships that I don't need a partner."* But what he felt, apparently, overrode what he thought.

**Gauri Spratt**, 47, works in the wellness and beauty space and has a seven-year-old son, **Quinn**, from a previous marriage. She is originally from Bangalore. And her family backstory carries a thread that reads like a novel: her grandfather, **Philip Spratt**, was a British-born Communist who came to India in the 1920s — not to trade or to rule, but to fight alongside Indians for their own independence. He crossed an ocean and chose India over Britain. There is something almost poetically fitting about his granddaughter now making India her home again, in the most personal sense of the word.

Since Aamir introduced Gauri publicly at his 60th birthday celebrations last year, the two have been spotted together with increasing ease. They have been living together as a family for over a year now. The wedding, as described by those close to the couple, will be a simple signing — no designer mandap, no three-day destination affair. Just a private moment made official.

## A Weekend of Reunions

The timing is exquisite. Tomorrow — Saturday, June 13 — Aamir is hosting a massive reunion bash for the entire cast and crew of **Lagaan**, his career-defining magnum opus that turns 25 on June 15. The film has just re-released in theaters across India for a special three-day run. The party, set at a five-star Mumbai hotel, reportedly includes not just the principal cast but every unit member who worked on the film.

And in August, his latest production **Batwara** — starring **Sunny Deol**, **Preity Zinta**, and directed by **Rajkumar Santoshi** — hits theaters on Independence Day weekend. Twenty-five years after *Gadar* and *Lagaan* split the nation's loyalties at the box office, Aamir and Sunny are finally on the same side.

For NRI audiences who grew up watching Aamir evolve from the boy next door in *QSQT* to the perfectionist behind *Dangal* and *3 Idiots*, his personal journey now mirrors the arc his best characters have always followed — vulnerability, honest self-work, and the courage to start over. At 60, with three children across two previous marriages, a quiet partner from Bangalore, and a film that just re-entered cinemas a quarter-century later, Aamir Khan is not so much starting a new chapter as he is finally writing the one he always wanted.

The wedding is on July 5. The reunion starts this weekend. And Bollywood has a love story it didn't have to cast.
